title: By the dawn.
subtitle: An oath by the morning that ends every night
then: Revealed when {trap}the new Muslims of Makkah had begun to be persecuted.{/trap} Ali, Ibn Abbas and others said the dawn is the morning. Ibn Kathir says these oaths point to {idea}times of worship and the worship itself{/idea} done by Allah's humble servants.
now: The alarm at Fajr, still dark outside. The night shift nurse watching the window go grey. A hard season that feels like it will never end. {idea}Dawn has never missed a day.{/idea} The One who sends it keeps the rest of His order too.
old: My hard night will just keep going.
new: The One who never misses a dawn is running my life too.
try: Watch the sky at Fajr time once this week, even for one minute after praying.

title: By the ten nights.
subtitle: The first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah
then: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Zubayr, Mujahid and others said these are {idea}the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said there are {reward}no days in which good deeds are more beloved to Allah than these days.{/reward}
now: You plan your year around the Black Friday sale, the bonus month, the summer trip. {reward}Allah has His own season of best deals.{/reward} It comes every year, and most people let it pass like any other week.
old: Special days are for other, more religious people.
new: Allah gives me seasons where small deeds weigh more. I can use them.
try: Put the first ten days of next Dhul-Hijjah in your phone calendar now with a reminder.

title: By the even and the odd.
subtitle: Two sacred days at the height of Hajj
then: A hadith mentions that {idea}the odd is the day of Arafah, on the ninth, and the even is the day of Sacrifice, on the tenth.{/idea} Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said the same. Ibn Kathir notes other opinions exist too.
now: Your days feel like a blur of numbers: date, shift, deadline. {idea}The verse swears by two dates that are full of worship.{/idea} It asks which of your days will be remembered for something you did for Allah.
old: Dates on a calendar are just numbers to get through.
new: Some days are sworn by because of the worship in them. Mine can hold worship too.
try: Choose one day this week and plan one extra act of worship for it.

title: By the night as it slips away.
subtitle: The night always moves on
then: Ibn Abbas said: {idea}when it goes away.{/idea} Abdullah ibn Zubayr said: {idea}as some parts of it remove other parts.{/idea} The surah opens with dawn and closes its oaths with night leaving, a picture of {idea}the regular order of night and day.{/idea}
now: You lie awake at 3am with a worry. The night feels endless. Then the birds start. {idea}No night has ever stayed.{/idea} The same order that moves the night is the order that will bring every deed to account.
old: Time just slips by without meaning anything.
new: Every passing night is part of an order with a purpose.
try: Before you sleep tonight, spend one minute thinking about how you used the day that just passed.

title: Is that not enough for anyone with sense?
subtitle: The oaths are for the mind that holds itself back
then: Ibn Kathir: hijr is {idea}intellect, sound reasoning and understanding.{/idea} It is called hijr because {idea}it prevents a person from doing what does not befit him.{/idea} The same root names the Hijr beside the Kaaba, a boundary.
now: You are smart enough to pass exams and run a team. But can your mind stop you from sending the angry text, from the second helping of gossip? {idea}Real sense is the brake, not just the engine.{/idea}
old: Being intelligent means knowing a lot.
new: Being intelligent means my mind can hold me back from wrong.
try: Next time you are about to say something you will regret, pause for three breaths first.

title: Have you not seen what your Lord did with Ad?
subtitle: A nation that rejected its messenger Hud
then: Ad were {trap}rebellious, arrogant, deniers of His messengers.{/trap} Allah sent them Hud, saved him and the believers, and destroyed the rest with a violent wind. Ibn Kathir: their story is told {idea}so that the believers may learn a lesson.{/idea}
now: A documentary about ruined cities. You watch it with popcorn, then move on. {idea}The Quran tells these stories so you look at yourself:{/idea} where in your life are you ignoring a clear warning because you feel strong?
old: Stories of destroyed nations are just ancient history.
new: These stories are told so I check my own arrogance now.
try: Name one warning in your life you keep ignoring, and take one step to address it.

title: Iram, the people of the lofty pillars.
subtitle: The first Ad, who built on firm columns
then: Ibn Kathir: they lived in {reward}houses raised with firm pillars{/reward} and were the strongest people of their time. Hud reminded them of this blessing and told them to use it in obedience. Instead {trap}they said: who is mightier than us?{/trap}
now: Your strong body at the gym. Your title at work. Your bank balance. {idea}Every strength you have is a blessing with a job attached.{/idea} The question is whether you use it for Allah or to look down on people.
old: My strength and success are proof I am doing fine.
new: My strength is a gift, and its job is obedience, not boasting.
try: Use one strength you have today to help someone weaker, quietly.

title: No one like them had been created in the land.
subtitle: Their strength was unmatched in their time
then: Qatadah and Ibn Jarir said {idea}no tribe like them had been created in the land in their time.{/idea} Ibn Kathir calls this the correct view. Even so, they were brought down. Allah who created them was mightier than them.
now: The company that was "too big to fail." The champion who was unbeatable for ten years. {trap}Being number one has never protected anyone.{/trap} {idea}Only the One who made you is greater than all of it.{/idea}
old: If I am at the top, I am safe.
new: Even the strongest were made by One stronger. Safety is with Him.
try: When you feel proud of being the best at something today, say: it is from Allah.

title: Thamud, who carved homes out of rock.
subtitle: Skill and engineering that did not save them
then: Ibn Abbas said: {idea}they carved and hewed the rocks.{/idea} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse where they are told: {trap}you carve houses in the mountains with great skill.{/trap} Their skill was real. It did not stop what came.
now: The extension on your house. The career you engineered step by step. The savings plan carved in stone. {idea}Good things to build.{/idea} But they are not a shelter from Allah's judgement. Only obedience is.
old: If I build well and plan well, I am secure.
new: Skill is a gift. Security is in obeying the One who gave it.
try: Look at one thing you have built or planned and ask Allah to put blessing in it.

title: And Pharaoh, the man of the stakes.
subtitle: Power enforced through armies and cruelty
then: Ibn Abbas said {trap}the stakes are the armies who enforced his commands.{/trap} Others, like Mujahid, said he used to fasten people to stakes as punishment. Either way, the image is of power held by force.
now: You may not rule a country, but you may run a team, a classroom, a household. {trap}Fear works fast.{/trap} {idea}The question is how the people under your authority feel when you walk in.{/idea}
old: Being firm and feared is how you keep control.
new: Power held by fear is the Pharaoh pattern. I want the opposite.
try: Do one kind thing today for someone you have authority over: a child, a staff member, a student.

title: All of them crossed every limit in the land.
subtitle: What Ad, Thamud and Pharaoh shared
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}they rebelled, were arrogant, and went about making corruption in the land and harming the people.{/trap} Strength, stone and armies were not the sin. {idea}Using them to cross limits was.{/idea}
now: The extra hour you take from your employer. The rule you bend because no one checks. The temper you let loose because you can. {idea}Transgression starts small and personal.{/idea}
old: Crossing limits is what tyrants do, not people like me.
new: Any limit I cross because I can is the same seed.
try: Notice one small limit you tend to cross, and keep it today.

title: And they spread corruption everywhere.
subtitle: Transgression always spills onto other people
then: After crossing limits, the next step: {trap}they increased the corruption{/trap}, making mischief in the land and {trap}harming the people.{/trap} Wrong never stays private for long.
now: One person cuts corners at work and soon the whole team does. One cruel joke in the group chat and everyone joins in. {idea}What you allow in yourself spreads to the people around you.{/idea} So does good.
old: My bad habits only affect me.
new: What I do spreads. I can spread good instead.
try: Start one small good trend today: a kind word, an honest answer, a tidy shared space.

title: So your Lord poured a punishment on them.
subtitle: When corruption peaked, the reckoning came

row.title: nothing happened, so it is fine

then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}He sent down a torment from the sky that could not be repelled{/trap} from the criminals. The people of Makkah, who were persecuting the believers, heard this as a {idea}clear warning about where that road leads.{/idea}
now: You did something wrong last year and nothing happened. So you did it again. {idea}Silence is not approval. It is time given to turn back.{/idea} The verse is about them, and it is a mirror for you.
old: If nothing bad has happened, it must be fine.
new: Delay is a chance to turn back, not a sign of approval.
try: Seek forgiveness today for one wrong that you got away with.

title: Your Lord is always watching.
subtitle: He hears, He sees, and He will judge with justice
then: Ibn Abbas said: {idea}He hears and He sees.{/idea} Ibn Kathir: He watches over His creation and will reward each {reward}based on what each of them strove for{/reward}, judging with justice. For persecuted believers in Makkah, this was comfort.
now: You are treated unfairly at work and no one notices. You are patient with a hard relative and no one sees. {reward}Your Lord is watching, and He is just.{/reward} The ones who wronged you are seen too.
old: No one sees what I go through or what I do right.
new: Allah is watching, so nothing I suffer or do is lost.
try: When you feel unseen today, whisper: Allah sees this.

title: When given plenty, he says: my Lord honored me.
subtitle: Mistaking a test of wealth for a sign of favor
then: Ibn Kathir: Allah refutes the belief that {trap}abundant provision means He honors you.{/trap} {idea}It is a trial and a test.{/idea} He gives wealth to those He loves and those He does not. The surah now turns from past nations to everyday human nature.
now: The promotion comes through. The house sale goes well. You post #blessed. {idea}It may be a blessing, and it is certainly a test:{/idea} will you thank Allah and use it well, or just feel better than others?
old: When life is going well, it means Allah is pleased with me.
new: Good times are a test of gratitude, not a certificate of favor.
try: Thank Allah for one good thing this week, then give a small part of it away.

title: When money is tight, he says: my Lord humiliated me.
subtitle: Mistaking a test of hardship for rejection
then: Ibn Kathir: if Allah tests a person by limiting his sustenance, {trap}he believes Allah is humiliating him.{/trap} Allah withholds from those He loves and those He does not. {idea}The point is to obey Him in either case:{/idea} thank Him when rich, be patient when poor.
now: Payday comes and the bills eat it all. Friends go on holiday and you check prices you cannot afford. {trap}You start to feel forgotten by Allah.{/trap} {idea}Tight months are also a test, not a verdict.{/idea}
old: When money is short, Allah must have turned away from me.
new: Hardship is a test of patience. It does not mean He rejected me.
try: In a tight moment today, say Alhamdulillah for one thing you still have.

title: No. The real problem: you do not honor the orphan.
subtitle: The test was never about how much you had
then: Allah says {idea}No!{/idea} to both claims, then names the real failure: {trap}you do not honor the orphan.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes it contains the command to honor him, and the Prophet ﷺ said the orphan's guardian {reward}and I will be like these two in Paradise{/reward}, holding two fingers together.
now: You spend hours thinking about whether your life is going well. Meanwhile there is a child in your extended family whose father died, and you have not called in a year. {idea}The test was what you did for them.{/idea}
old: My test is whether I am rich or poor.
new: My test is what I do for the vulnerable with what I have.
try: Contact or support one orphan, or a charity that cares for orphans, this week.

title: And you do not push each other to feed the poor.
subtitle: A community that never encourages giving
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}they do not command that the poor and needy be treated with kindness, nor encourage each other to do so.{/trap} The verse does not only blame not giving. It blames {idea}a whole circle that never talks about it.{/idea}
now: Your friends' group chat talks about restaurants, phones, holidays. When did it last share a food bank appeal? {idea}One message from you can change what your circle sees as normal.{/idea}
old: Feeding the poor is a private matter between me and Allah.
new: I can also be the one who reminds others to feed the poor.
try: Share one way to feed someone in need with a friend or family group today.

title: You swallow inheritance whole, by any means.
subtitle: Greed with no care for lawful or unlawful
then: Ibn Kathir: the turath is {idea}the inheritance{/idea}, and they devour it {trap}however they can get it, whether lawful or forbidden.{/trap} Right after neglecting orphans, the verse names how their shares were often eaten.
now: A parent dies and the family group chat goes quiet, then tense. Who gets the house? Who took the gold? {trap}Grief turns into grabbing.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks you to slow down and take only what is truly yours.{/idea}
old: If I can get more of the family money, why not?
new: Only what is rightfully mine is worth taking. The rest is a burden.
try: If there is a family money matter in your life, make dua to be fair in it.

title: And you love money with an endless love.
subtitle: The root under all four failures
then: Ibn Kathir: they love wealth {trap}in abundance, and this increases some of them in their wickedness.{/trap} This verse names the root under the neglect of the orphan, the poor, and the greed over inheritance.
now: Checking your bank app ten times a day. Feeling a pinch every time you give. Lying awake planning the next purchase. {idea}Money is not the problem. Loving it without limit is.{/idea}
old: Wanting more money is just being responsible.
new: When money lives in my heart, it pushes out mercy for others.
try: Give away a small amount today that you will slightly feel, and notice the heart loosen.

title: No. When the earth is pounded flat, again and again.
subtitle: Everything you built on is leveled
then: The No here answers the love of wealth before it. Ibn Kathir: {trap}the earth and the mountains will be flattened, leveled and made even{/trap}, and {idea}the creatures will rise from their graves for their Lord.{/idea}
now: The property you saved for. The land your family fought over. The office tower you work in. {trap}All of it, flat.{/trap} {idea}The only things that stand up on that Day are you and what you did.{/idea}
old: What I own is solid and will always be there.
new: The earth itself will be leveled. My deeds are what remain.
try: Look at one thing you own that you value most and ask: what deed can I do with it?

title: Your Lord comes, and the angels, row upon row.
subtitle: The session of Judgement begins

row.title: I will talk my way out

then: Ibn Kathir: people will ask messenger after messenger to intercede, and each will say he cannot, until they reach Muhammad ﷺ, who says: {reward}I will do it.{/reward} Then {idea}Allah comes for the Judgement as He wills{/idea}, and the angels line up, row on row.
now: You have stood in a courtroom, a job interview, or outside an exam hall, and felt your legs go weak. {idea}That Day is bigger than all of them.{/idea} {reward}Sending salawat on the Prophet ﷺ is preparing for it.{/reward}
old: I will manage on my own when the time comes.
new: That Day, even the greatest messengers wait. I prepare now and send salawat.
try: Send salawat on the Prophet ﷺ ten times today.

title: That Day man remembers, but it is too late to help.
subtitle: Remembering after the chance has gone
then: Hell is brought near, and Ibn Kathir: man will remember {idea}his deeds, what he did in his past and recent times.{/idea} {trap}How can remembrance then benefit him?{/trap}
now: You keep saying you will sort your prayers out when life calms down. You remember, nod, and forget. {idea}Today the remembering still works.{/idea} One day it will only be regret.
old: I know I should change. I will get around to it.
new: Remembering only helps while I can still act on it. That is now.
try: Act on one thing you remembered today that you have been meaning to do for Allah.

title: If only I had sent something ahead for my life.
subtitle: The real life was the one coming next
then: Ibn Kathir: the disobedient will regret his sins, and {reward}the obedient will wish he had done more.{/reward} A Companion said that even someone who prostrated from birth to old age would think it little on that Day, and wish to come back to earn more.
now: You send money ahead to a new flat before you move. You pack a bag ahead of a trip. {idea}The verse calls the next life my life.{/idea} What have you sent ahead for it this week?
old: This life is my real life. The next one is an extra.
new: The next life is my life. I send things ahead for it now.
try: Send one deed ahead today: a charity, a prayer, a kindness, with that intention.

title: That Day no one punishes as He punishes.
subtitle: The seriousness of disobeying Allah
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}there is no one more severely punished than those whom Allah punishes for disobeying Him.{/trap} Coming after the regret of verse 24, the verse is short and sober.
now: You fear your manager's email, your parents' disappointment, what people will say. You work hard to avoid those. {idea}The verse asks you to fear disobeying Allah more than any of them{/idea}, and to run to His mercy now.
old: What people think of me is what I mostly fear.
new: Disobeying Allah is the thing to fear, and His mercy is open now.
try: Ask Allah's forgiveness today for one specific thing, and then do one good deed after it.

title: And no one binds as He binds.
subtitle: Those who were free to do wrong are held fast
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}none is more severely bound{/trap} than those the keepers of Hell bind, and this is {trap}for the criminals and wrongdoers.{/trap} Pharaoh and the others of verses 6-12 moved freely through the land. That freedom ends.
now: You tell yourself you are free: no one tells you what to do. But the habit at night, the anger, the spending, already have you tied up. {idea}Real freedom is choosing obedience while you still can.{/idea}
old: Freedom means no limits on what I do.
new: Obeying Allah now is what keeps me free on that Day.
try: Break one small habit that controls you, just for today.

title: O soul at peace.
subtitle: The voice that speaks to the tranquil soul
then: After the harshness, a gentle call. Ibn Kathir: this is {reward}the pure and tranquil soul, always at rest and abiding by the truth.{/reward} It contrasts with the person of verses 15-16 whose mood rose and fell with his money.
now: Your mood depends on your bank balance, your likes, your boss's tone. {reward}A soul at peace is not shaken by those.{/reward} {idea}It is built slowly, prayer by prayer, remembrance by remembrance.{/idea}
old: Peace will come when my circumstances settle.
new: Peace is a state of soul built with Allah, whatever my circumstances.
try: Sit for two minutes after your next prayer and just repeat Allah's name quietly.

title: Come back to your Lord, pleased and pleasing to Him.
subtitle: A return where both sides are content
then: Ibn Kathir: return {reward}to His company, His reward and what He has prepared.{/reward} Well-pleased within itself, pleased with Allah, and He pleased with it. Ibn Abbas reported Abu Bakr said: {reward}there is nothing better than this!{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ replied: it will be said to you.
now: Coming home after a long trip and the door opens, and someone is glad to see you. {reward}Now imagine Allah pleased to see you{/reward}, and you pleased with everything He gave. That is the welcome this verse describes.
old: Going back to Allah is something to dread.
new: Going back to Allah can be a homecoming, with both sides pleased.
try: Ask Allah today: make me pleased with You and You pleased with me.

title: Enter among My servants.
subtitle: Belonging to the company of Allah's servants
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}among their ranks.{/reward} Earlier the surah told of nations who wanted to be above everyone. It ends with a soul honored by being {idea}one of Allah's servants{/idea}, standing among them.
now: You want the VIP list, the corner office, the blue tick. {idea}The highest list there is: My servants.{/idea} You join it by serving Him here, in the rows of the masjid, shoulder to shoulder.
old: Honor means standing above the crowd.
new: The best honor is being counted among Allah's servants.
try: Pray one prayer in congregation this week, standing shoulder to shoulder.

title: And enter My Paradise.
subtitle: The final word to the soul at peace
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}this will be said at the time of death and on the Day of Judgement{/reward}, like the angels giving glad tidings to the believer. The surah that began with dawn ends with {reward}My Paradise{/reward}, a garden Allah calls His own.
now: The surah walked you through ruined nations, the pull of money, and the Day itself. It ends with an invitation, not a threat. {reward}Enter My Paradise.{/reward} {idea}Every prayer, every fed orphan, is walking toward that door.{/idea}
old: Paradise feels too far for someone like me.
new: Allah invites the soul at peace into His own Paradise. I can walk toward it.
try: Ask Allah tonight for Paradise by name, in your own words, three times.
